newsitem.title: RWANDA: Zaire town of Goma enjoys respite from battles.
newsitem.headline: Zaire town of Goma enjoys respite from battles.

text.p: The east Zaire town of Goma, which suffered fierce battles on its fringes on Thursday, was quieter on Friday.

Reuters correspondent Christian Jennings saw 12 rockets fired from multiple rocket launchers land between five and 10 km (three to six miles) north of Goma airport early on Friday, but by 0700 GMT he said there was only sporadic automatic arms fire to be heard.

"It is quiet right now, there is no firing or shooting. it is really very peaceful," U.N. refugee agency spokesman Panos Moumtzis said by telephone from inside Goma city just across the border from Gisenyi, Rwanda.

At the Zaire-Rwanda border crossing, the atmosphere on Friday morning was surreal. Five Zairean soldiers at the border post danced naked, waving automatic weapons, chanting and sprinkling water on each other.

Goma is the administrative centre for relief operations for 1.1. million Rwandan Hutu refugees in eastern Zaire. Many of them have been on the run from fighting between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops for at least a week and Moumtzis said it was simply not known what state these refugees were in.
The refugees now live in a constant state of panic. "At one point yesterday we had refugees on the road walking in both directions," said Moumtzis.
"They are really panicking. They are very scared. They do not know where to go.
